open_points.subject: public_op:canonical_values.fit_port_value
open_points.text: "Inputs One Port M01 and one candidate ... size bound applying to the whole value ... or for a many file port ... each checked ... against the per-file size bound."
open_points.question: Which concrete size bound(s) must fit_port_value apply in each call context, and how are those bounds provided to it?
options: Add explicit size-limit arguments (value_limit_bytes, file_limit_bytes) to the operation input
Make callers enforce size ceilings separately and have fit_port_value check only presence/carriage/schema
Derive limits implicitly from global release ceilings inside fit_port_value
open_points.default_guess: Make callers enforce size ceilings separately and keep fit_port_value limited to structural/schema checks.

open_points.subject: public_op:service_invoker.prepare_request pre-send failure detail
open_points.kind: insufficient discriminant for required error codes
open_points.text: "Outputs ... or the first pre-send failure" with distinct details including "instance_not_selected" and "instance_address_missing"; input is "A ManifestOperation M10 with instance facts ..."
open_points.question: How must prepare_request distinguish "instance_not_selected" from "instance_address_missing" when instance facts are missing/absent in ManifestOperation data?
options: Require an explicit selected-instance-presence flag/name in prepare_request input
Collapse both conditions to one detail code
Infer from partial ManifestOperation fields (e.g., base_url/required_headers presence)
open_points.default_guess: Infer from field presence (if no instance facts at all -> instance_not_selected; if instance selected but base_url missing -> instance_address_missing).

open_points.subject: public_op:functions.read_slot output contract
open_points.text: "A serving implementation without a verdict over its contract version's current corpus is marked so explicitly, not left to be inferred (A04 rule 7)."
open_points.question: What exact output fact marks this condition, so callers can rely on one stable machine-readable indicator?
options: A dedicated boolean on each implementation entry (e.g., serving_without_current_corpus_verdict)
A dedicated status enum value in the implementation summary
No dedicated field; rely on clients to infer by comparing activation and verdict groups
open_points.default_guess: Add a dedicated boolean flag on each implementation entry in read_slot output.
